title: Size Auto from bounded widths and the Linux merge crossover
question: Can cheap width evidence, known merge boundaries, or contention measurements improve automatic resource choices?
summary: Hosted shuffles can use four bounded interior width samples and keep the starting tier under pressure. Linux shuffles can use matching Analyze to target 384 MiB in the measured extra-merge band. Retain the automatic worker policy and bounded-writer opt-in.

workloads: Chromium plain CSV uniform and skewed composed shuffles, including quoted and above-range controls.
Linux file-backed 2.00–4.01 GiB uniform shuffles at multiple budgets.
Two concurrent native jobs testing gzip shuffle publication workers and 12- or 96-group writers.

validation.summary: Verified full record contents, conservation, caps, grouping, applicable stable ordering, publication and cleanup. Tested the actual resource targets with the integrated planner and matched Analyze.

limitations: One physical host, Linux in WSL, native Windows on NTFS, and Chromium using OPFS.
Small synthetic cells. Some independent experiments overlapped, and sampled widths can miss shape changes or fall inside a quoted field.
exclusions: Automatic starts of full Analyze, Windows merge-tier promotion, and default publication strategy promotion.
reopen_when: Calibrate inexpensive features that predict a materially profitable full Analyze beyond the sampled plain CSV cases.
